Update three plugin subagent definitions — vector:challenger, canon:audit-spec, and
lambda:implementer — to catch architectural/semantic-model defects (sibling drift across
trait implementers, cross-layer round-trip gaps) at spec/plan time instead of after code
is written. Full rationale and sourced findings: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/8dffec3b-bc4b-4664-a5eb-602c92d40b78

These are Claude Code plugin agent definitions, not part of any project repo — locate them
first (likely markdown files with YAML frontmatter, under wherever `/plugin` installed the
marketplace on this machine — search by agent name, don't assume a path). If you can't find
editable source for one of them, say so plainly instead of reporting success.

Read each target file fully before editing — match its existing structure, tone, and format
exactly. Don't restructure anything unrelated.

Make exactly these three edits:

1. vector:challenger — add an 8th review dimension, "interface-incompleteness": when a task
   modifies one implementer of a shared trait/interface/protocol, the plan must cover every
   other known implementer or explicitly state why not. This check must be backed by a
   deterministic pre-scan (grep/AST enumeration of implementers) run before the agent's own
   reasoning — not an LLM asked to "remember" siblings.

2. canon:audit-spec — add a 6th audit dimension, "boundary round-trip coverage": when a
   criterion introduces or changes a field on a type that another spec persists, serializes,
   or transmits, that far-side spec needs a matching round-trip criterion, or the gap must be
   named on purpose.

3. lambda:implementer — add a default-posture instruction: when a criterion involves a value
   that can be absent, wrong, or stale — especially at a process/crate/serialization boundary
   — prefer a sum type / discriminated union / Result-shaped representation over a raw
   value-plus-boolean pair, in whatever language the task is in. Escalate to canon:architect
   only when a single-instance fix can't achieve this within the task's own scope.

Show me the diff for each file before calling this done.

Explicitly out of scope — flag as a possible follow-up, don't build it now: the two-gate
human checkpoint protocol (a workflow habit I'll apply manually) and loop-back automation
(proof→architect on ≥2× recurrence, periodic drift-checker/audit-backlog runs).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# For each plugin, checks that plugin.json's version, the README's
# **Version:** line, the CHANGELOG's top entry, and marketplace.json's
# per-plugin version all agree. These four are updated by hand on every
# bump and have drifted before (fixed across 4 plugins in v3.1.0) —
# nothing structural stopped it from happening again.
#
# Usage: scripts/check-versions.sh

set -euo pipefail
script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib/report.sh
source "$script_dir/lib/report.sh"
cd "$script_dir/.."

fail=0
count=0

for plugin_json in plugins/*/plugin.json; do
  dir="$(dirname "$plugin_json")"
  id="$(basename "$dir")"
  count=$((count + 1))

  pj_version="$(jq -r '.version' "$plugin_json")"
  readme_version="$(grep -oE '\*\*Version:\*\* *[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' "$dir/README.md" | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' || true)"
  changelog_version="$(grep -oE '^## \[[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' "$dir/CHANGELOG.md" | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' || true)"
  marketplace_version="$(jq -r --arg id "$id" '.plugins[] | select(.id == $id) | .version' marketplace.json)"

  mismatches=()
  [[ -z "$readme_version" ]] && mismatches+=("README: no **Version:** line found")
  [[ -n "$readme_version" && "$readme_version" != "$pj_version" ]] && mismatches+=("README says $readme_version")
  [[ -z "$changelog_version" ]] && mismatches+=("CHANGELOG: no ## [x.y.z] entry found")
  [[ -n "$changelog_version" && "$changelog_version" != "$pj_version" ]] && mismatches+=("CHANGELOG says $changelog_version")
  [[ -z "$marketplace_version" ]] && mismatches+=("marketplace.json: no entry for id \"$id\"")
  [[ -n "$marketplace_version" && "$marketplace_version" != "$pj_version" ]] && mismatches+=("marketplace.json says $marketplace_version")

  if [[ ${#mismatches[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    echo "FAIL: $id (plugin.json: $pj_version)"
    for m in "${mismatches[@]}"; do
      echo "    $m"
    done
  fi
done

report_check "$fail" "$count" \
  "plugin(s), all versions agree across plugin.json/README/CHANGELOG/marketplace.json." \
  "plugin(s) have version drift. Fix and re-run."

9	### T7. Intent-Capture-to-Execution Discard ← highest impact
10	- **Signal:** A wide options object or validated config is constructed with user-specified fields (`dryRun`, `registry`, `tag`, `access`), but the function that performs the side effect accepts a narrower interface — those fields are never read at the execution boundary.
11	
12	```typescript
13	// ✗ BEFORE — tag and registry captured, silently dropped at the call site
14	interface PublishOptions {
15	  packageId: string
16	  version: string
17	  registry?: string  // user-specified
18	  tag?: string       // user-specified
19	}
20	
21	// Narrow parameter type — extra fields structurally compatible but never read
22	function publish(opts: { packageId: string; version: string }) {
23	  execSync(`npm publish`) // registry, tag never reach the command
24	}
25	
26	function run(opts: PublishOptions) {
27	  publish(opts) // TypeScript allows this; registry and tag are silently gone
28	}
29	
30	// ✓ AFTER — execution function accepts the full options type
31	function publish(opts: PublishOptions) {
32	  const args = ['npm', 'publish']
33	  if (opts.registry) args.push('--registry', opts.registry)
34	  if (opts.tag)      args.push('--tag', opts.tag)
35	  execSync(args.join(' '))
36	}
37	```
38	- **Search:**
39	  1. Find options/config types — interfaces or types matching `*Options`, `*Config`, `*Params`, `*Payload`, `*Args`.
40	  2. Find construction sites where the wide type is built with user-provided values.
41	  3. Find the execution function — check its parameter type and what it actually reads.
42	  4. Flag any field present in the constructed object but absent from the execution function's parameter type or body.
43	- **Risk:** User intent (dry-run, private registry, access level) is silently overridden by a hardcoded default.
44	- **False positive check:** Is the field explicitly documented as unused at the call site?
45	- **Verdict signal:** Confirmable when the field is absent from the execution function's parameter type, or present in the type but not read in the body. Dismissible only when the field is explicitly read and forwarded to the subprocess or external call.
46	
47	### T10. Error Suppression & Downgrade ← distinct from T2
48	- **Signal:** A catch block or rejection handler that swallows the error without signaling failure to the caller. The outer call resolves or returns successfully even though the operation failed.
49	  - `.catch(() => {})` or `.catch((_) => undefined)` — empty or null-returning handler
50	  - `try { ... } catch { }` — catch with no body (TS 4.0+ allows omitting the binding entirely)
51	  - `try { ... } catch (e) { console.log(e) }` — only logging, not re-throwing or returning a failure signal
52	- **Grep patterns:**
53	  - `\.catch\(\s*[(_)]\s*=>\s*\{?\s*\}?\s*\)` — empty or trivially-returning catch handler
54	  - `catch\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{\s*\}` — empty catch body
55	  - `catch\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{\s*console\.\w+` — logging-only catch
56	- **Risk:** Callers receive a resolved promise or a non-throwing return believing the operation succeeded. The failure is invisible to monitoring, retry logic, and the caller's control flow.
57	- **False positive check:** Is the no-op explicitly documented as intentional? Is the error logged AND the caller notified via a return value or status field? If neither, it is suppression.
58	- **Distinguisher from T2 (Unhandled Promise Rejection):** T2 has no catch at all — the rejection propagates unhandled. T10 has a catch that actively hides the error from the caller.
59	- **Verdict signal:** Confirmable when the catch handler resolves or returns without signaling failure...

Each one closes a different stage of the same underlying failure — a value or shape that's correct in one place silently isn't in another:

- **auditor** catches it at the *data-model* level, before a plan exists — "this spec adds a field the store/wire spec never learns to round-trip."
- **challenger** catches it at the *plan* level, before code exists — "this plan touches one `impl` of a trait and never mentions its siblings."
- **implementer** catches it at the *code* level, as it's written — "this value can be absent/wrong/stale, so it becomes a sum type by construction, not a bool next to it that someone forgets to check."

If all three hold, the exact three real defects from the artifact's evidence table (unpropagated `ClaudeCodeAdapter` fix, `is_fully_priced` hardcoded on read-back, `tool_counts` never wired) get stopped one stage earlier than they were caught this time.

1	# Documentation Voice Reference
2	
3	Canonical voice standard for this repo: commit messages, PR bodies, changesets, release notes, and prose docs (READMEs, `basis`-scaffolded plugin docs). Succinct, engineering-focused, scannable. No AI slop.
4	
5	Agents load only the subset embedded in their own task reference file (`conventional-commits.md`, `github.md`, `changesets.md`) — see each for the operational rules. This file is the full standard, for humans and for `basis` when scaffolding new docs.
6	
7	Doc comments and inline code comments are a separate reader profile (a caller or a maintainer reading one line, not someone reading prose) — see `code-comments.md` for that operational subset instead.
8	
9	## Rules
10	
11	1. Lead with the conclusion. Answer before justification (inverted pyramid) — readers scan ~20-28% of page text, they don't read top to bottom.
12	2. Active voice, present tense, second person for instructions.
13	3. One idea per sentence. A sentence that keeps running is usually doing two jobs — stating something and hedging it, or the *what* and the *why* — split it instead of trimming words to make it fit.
14	4. Bullets or tables over paragraphs whenever the content is enumerable.
15	5. Separate *what changed* (factual, reference-like) from *why* (one sentence, no more) — don't blend them into one block.
16	6. State the mechanism, not the adjective. Numbers and behavior over "robust" / "powerful" / "seamless."
17	7. Cut hedge and filler qualifiers: "essentially," "basically," "in order to," "it's worth noting that."
18	8. Self-edit pass: after drafting, re-read once checking rule 5 (what/why blending) and the banned-word list specifically before output. Banned-word avoidance alone misses ~20% of slop without this pass.

37	
38	A changeset is one coherent, single-sentence-describable change — not a diff, and not a file/package/commit count. Bundling unrelated topics and fragmenting one coherent effort are equally real failure modes.

40	What belongs together, in order of how much weight the signal carries:
41	
42	1. **Shared `linked_spec`/`linked_plan`/`linked_requirement`** — a scope decision already made before the code existed, so it outweighs anything read from the diff. A testing push scoped as one requirement is one changeset even across every package.

44	3. **Shared cause read from the diff**, only absent 1 and 2: does one part exist *because of* another (one changeset), or would each have happened independently (separate changesets)? An "and" joining two unrelated things is two changesets.

1	# Conventional Commits Reference
2	
3	**Format:** `<type>(<scope>): <description>`
4	
5	Types: `feat` `fix` `docs` `style` `refactor` `test` `chore` `perf` `ci` `build` `revert`
6	
7	Breaking change: append `!` after type/scope, or add `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
8	
9	## Rules
10	
11	- Subject line: imperative mood, no period, under 72 characters
12	- Body (optional): explain the *why*, not the what. Do not artificially wrap lines — one paragraph per line, let the terminal/renderer soft-wrap.
13	- Footer: `BREAKING CHANGE: <description>`, `Fixes #123`, `Refs #456`
14	- Scope is optional; when used, it names the module or component
15	
16	## Examples
17	
18	```
19	feat(delta): add changeset generation skill
20	
21	fix(axiom): retry gate passes specific failure message to producer
22	
23	docs(shared): add conventional-commits reference
24	
25	refactor(proof): extract language detection into recon subagent
26	
27	feat!: rename bug-hunter-rust to proof
28	
29	BREAKING CHANGE: plugin ID changed from bug-hunter-rust to proof.
30	Update marketplace.json and skill trigger references.
31	```
32	
33	## Commit Message Body
34	
35	The body answers: why was this change needed? What problem does it solve?
36	
37	Don't describe what the code does (the diff shows that). Write what a reviewer needs to understand the intent.
38	
39	## Voice
40	
41	Active voice, imperative mood. If a sentence keeps running, it's usually doing two jobs — split it rather than trimming words to make it fit. No banned words: *delve, leverage, seamless, robust, elevate, foster, unlock, empower, testament, pivotal, showcase, meticulous, game-changer, utilize* (use "use"). Full standard: `shared/references/docs-voice.md`.

This session found and fixed three defect-class gaps in `canon`/`vector`/`lambda` (interface-incompleteness, boundary-round-trip, sum-type default posture), then a follow-up audit across the other six plugins (via four parallel background agents) plus my own direct reads of `basis`, `shared/constitution.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `.github/workflows/validate.yml` surfaced a broader pattern: **this repo has two parallel, disconnected conformance systems that don't stay in sync with each other or with the conventions they're supposed to enforce.**

Neither does either agent check "does every output status this agent can emit have SKILL.md routing" — the exact gap that shipped in `lambda` today and had to be hand-fixed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# For each plugin, checks that plugin.json's version, the README's
# **Version:** line, the CHANGELOG's top entry, and marketplace.json's
# per-plugin version all agree. These four are updated by hand on every
# bump and have drifted before (fixed across 4 plugins in v3.1.0) —
# nothing structural stopped it from happening again.
#
# Usage: scripts/check-versions.sh

set -euo pipefail
script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib/report.sh
source "$script_dir/lib/report.sh"
cd "$script_dir/.."

fail=0
count=0

for plugin_json in plugins/*/plugin.json; do
  dir="$(dirname "$plugin_json")"
  id="$(basename "$dir")"
  count=$((count + 1))

  pj_version="$(jq -r '.version' "$plugin_json")"
  readme_version="$(grep -oE '\*\*Version:\*\* *[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' "$dir/README.md" | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' || true)"
  changelog_version="$(grep -oE '^## \[[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' "$dir/CHANGELOG.md" | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' || true)"
  marketplace_version="$(jq -r --arg id "$id" '.plugins[] | select(.id == $id) | .version' marketplace.json)"

  mismatches=()
  [[ -z "$readme_version" ]] && mismatches+=("README: no **Version:** line found")
  [[ -n "$readme_version" && "$readme_version" != "$pj_version" ]] && mismatches+=("README says $readme_version")
  [[ -z "$changelog_version" ]] && mismatches+=("CHANGELOG: no ## [x.y.z] entry found")
  [[ -n "$changelog_version" && "$changelog_version" != "$pj_version" ]] && mismatches+=("CHANGELOG says $changelog_version")
  [[ -z "$marketplace_version" ]] && mismatches+=("marketplace.json: no entry for id \"$id\"")
  [[ -n "$marketplace_version" && "$marketplace_version" != "$pj_version" ]] && mismatches+=("marketplace.json says $marketplace_version")

  if [[ ${#mismatches[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    echo "FAIL: $id (plugin.json: $pj_version)"
    for m in "${mismatches[@]}"; do
      echo "    $m"
    done
  fi
done

report_check "$fail" "$count" \
  "plugin(s), all versions agree across plugin.json/README/CHANGELOG/marketplace.json." \
  "plugin(s) have version drift. Fix and re-run."
